course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Networks of Exchange
unit.description: Study how trade networks connected Afro-Eurasia through goods, technology, states, culture, and environmental change.

topic.title: The Mongol Empire and the Making of the Modern World
topic.summary: How steppe state building created the largest contiguous empire and reshaped trade, communication, and cultural transfer.

framework.name: InSPECT
framework.title: Use InSPECT to choose your evidence
framework.intro: A fact can connect to more than one lens. Choose the lens that helps answer the prompt.
framework.sourceNote: Based on the class Early Religions + InSPECT slides, pages 5-17.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

questions.prompt: Which factor most directly helped Chinggis Khan build a large steppe empire?
choices: He combined alliances, military organization, mobility, and the incorporation of conquered expertise
He replaced mounted warfare with permanent naval fleets
He inherited a unified bureaucratic empire from China
He ended competition among groups by banning all local leaders
questions.explanation: Mongol expansion relied on political consolidation, mounted mobility, organization, and adaptation rather than inherited Chinese rule or naval power.

questions.prompt: Why did horse-based mobility matter to Mongol expansion?

It let armies move, scout, and coordinate across large distances quickly

It prevented the empire from using local administrators
questions.explanation: Mobility increased operational speed and range. It did not eliminate siege warfare or administration.

questions.explanation: The mechanism is increased contact and mobility, not a universal speed or single intentional cause.

questions.prompt: Which thesis best answers how the Mongols affected larger patterns of continuity and change?
choices: They erased every earlier institution and created a completely new world
They caused only continuity because no region changed
They changed culture but never affected politics or trade
They changed political control and intensified connections while older regional institutions and inequalities persisted
questions.explanation: The strongest thesis balances political change and intensified connectivity with persistence and uneven outcomes.
